name: Question 2
worked_solution:
For this integral we choose $u=2{x}^{4}+4$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2{x}^{4}+4$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ |  |  |
| $8{x}^{3}$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}$ | $+$ | $\frac{(2{x}^{4}+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}$ |
| $24{x}^{2}$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}$ | $-$ | $\frac{8{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}$ |
| $48x$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{27}$ | $+$ | $-\frac{8{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}$ |
| $48$ | $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{81}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{16x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{27}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{243}$ | $+$ | $\frac{16\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{81}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2{x}^{4}+4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(2{x}^{4}+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{8{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}-\frac{8{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}-\frac{16x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{27}+\frac{16\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{81}+C \\  & =(54{x}^{4}-72{x}^{2}+124)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{81}+(24{x}^{3}-16x)\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{27}+C\end{aligned}
$$
